blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A billing job declares `Supplier<Invoice> draft = () -> invoices.newDraft(customerId);`, where newDraft() creates and returns an empty invoice. It then calls `draft.get().addLine(line)` for each of three order lines, and finally `invoices.save(draft.get())`. What does save() receive?

options.text: An invoice with all three lines, since the supplier hands back the invoice its first get() made
options.says: a Supplier keeps nothing between calls; each get() runs the body again

options.text: An empty invoice, since each get() ran newDraft() again and returned a different invoice
options.says: each get() ran newDraft(), so each line went to a draft of its own and save() received a fourth, empty one

options.text: An invoice with all three lines, since newDraft() ran once, when the lambda was assigned
options.says: creating the lambda runs nothing; the body runs on each get()

options.text: An invoice with only the last line, since each get() swaps a new invoice into the supplier
options.says: a Supplier has no field to hold an invoice in; each get() returns whatever the body returns

origin.section: A Supplier Runs Its Body on Every get() and Remembers Nothing

questions.stem: A product catalog was memoized with a synchronized block. A teammate replaces it with `AtomicReference<Catalog> cached`, where get() returns `cached.get()` if it is non-null and otherwise runs `cached.compareAndSet(null, loadCatalog())` and returns `cached.get()`. Ten request threads call get() at startup while the first loadCatalog() is still running. What changes?

options.text: loadCatalog() can run in several threads, but all callers return one catalog, since one result is stored
options.says: the compareAndSet memo keeps one result and still loads twice under contention

options.text: loadCatalog() still runs once, since compareAndSet is atomic and lets only one thread past the null check
options.says: compareAndSet decides which result is kept; every thread that found null has already called loadCatalog() by then

options.text: loadCatalog() can run in several threads, and each returns the catalog it loaded, since no lock orders them
options.says: each caller returns cached.get() after its compareAndSet, which is the first result stored

options.text: loadCatalog() still runs once, but threads can return different catalogs, since only the stored one is shared
options.says: the load can run more than once, and every caller returns cached.get(), the one result that was kept

origin.section: A Memo Written as Check-Then-Compute Loads Twice When Two Threads Arrive Together

questions.stem: A `Keys` class keeps a signing key in a nested class: `private static final class Holder { static final PrivateKey KEY = vault.fetch(); }`, read through `Keys.key()`. After a pod restart the vault is unreachable for three seconds, and the first request's call to Keys.key() fails. The vault answers again from the fourth second. What does a call to Keys.key() at the tenth second do?

options.text: It returns the key, since the JVM reruns the nested class's initialiser on its next use
options.says: a class whose initialiser threw is marked as failed and never initialised again in that JVM

options.text: It throws ExceptionInInitializerError, since the JVM keeps the first failure and rethrows it on each use
options.says: only the first use throws ExceptionInInitializerError; later uses throw NoClassDefFoundError

options.text: It returns the key, since a failed initialiser leaves the class unloaded and the next use loads it
options.says: class initialisation is not retried after it threw

options.text: It throws NoClassDefFoundError, since the JVM marked the class as failed and won't rerun its initialiser
options.says: the first use threw ExceptionInInitializerError; every later use throws NoClassDefFoundError until the process restarts

origin.section: A Safe Memo Chooses What It Pays: a Lock, Class Initialisation, or Startup Time

questions.stem: A service handles requests on a fixed pool of platform threads. Each request calls `digest.get()` once, where `ThreadLocal<MessageDigest> digest = ThreadLocal.withInitial(() -> newSha256())`. Over an hour the service handles tens of thousands of requests, and every pool thread takes some of them. How often did newSha256() run?

options.text: Once per pool thread, since withInitial calls the supplier on a thread's first get() and keeps that result
options.says: one value per thread, made on that thread's first get()

options.text: Once per request, since withInitial calls the supplier on every get() and returns the new digest
options.says: the ThreadLocal keeps the first result for the thread; later get() calls on it return the same object

options.text: Once in total, since withInitial calls the supplier when the ThreadLocal is created and shares that result
options.says: withInitial calls the supplier on each thread's first get(), and each thread keeps its own

options.text: Once per pool thread plus once more, since withInitial also calls the supplier when the ThreadLocal is created
options.says: nothing runs when the ThreadLocal is created; the supplier runs on a thread's first get()

origin.section: A Factory Supplier Must Return a New Object on Every Call

questions.stem: A metrics library offers `void gauge(String name, Supplier<Double> reading)`. Your code has `DoubleSupplier heapUsed = () -> rt.totalMemory() - rt.freeMemory();` and calls `gauge("heap", heapUsed)`. What happens?

options.text: It compiles, since DoubleSupplier extends Supplier<Double> and its getAsDouble() stands in for get()
options.says: the primitive suppliers are separate interfaces, not subtypes of Supplier

options.text: It doesn't compile, since DoubleSupplier is a separate interface that doesn't extend Supplier<Double>
options.says: the call is a type error; heapUsed::getAsDouble adapts it, boxing each value

options.text: It compiles, since the compiler boxes a DoubleSupplier into a Supplier<Double> as it boxes a double into a Double
options.says: boxing applies to primitive values, not to interface types

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a Supplier<Double> can't be built from a lambda whose body yields a primitive double
options.says: a lambda or method reference returning double is a Supplier<Double>; its value is boxed

origin.section: IntSupplier and Its Siblings Return Primitives and Are Not Suppliers

concepts: A compareAndSet memo keeps one result for every caller but can still run the load more than once.
A Supplier runs its body on every get() and keeps no result, so creating it runs nothing and each call can return a new object.
A holder class loads once through class initialisation, but a failed initialiser makes every later use throw NoClassDefFoundError until restart.
IntSupplier, LongSupplier, DoubleSupplier and BooleanSupplier are separate interfaces, not subtypes of Supplier, and are adapted with a method reference.
ThreadLocal.withInitial calls its supplier on each thread's first get() and keeps the result for that thread.
